news.title: FOCUS research accepted at IEEE S&P 2026
news.summary: Research on evading intrusion detectors through intelligent context distortion.
paragraphs: The paper “A Context is Worth a Thousand Lies” was accepted at the 2026 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy.

Magdy Nasr, Vansh Rastogi and Azadeh Tabiban investigate adversarial context in intrusion detection. Their framework, Contorter, examines how context can expose weaknesses in provenance-based detectors.
The publication and public code provide the full method and evaluation.

news.title: URGP funding for intrusion detection research
news.summary: Support for research on AI-based detection against AI-equipped attackers.
paragraphs: The University Research Grants Program (URGP) is supporting FOCUS research on intrusion detection against attackers that use AI.
The lab announced the funding in February 2025.

news.title: NSERC Discovery Grant supports provenance research
news.summary: Funding for provenance research in interconnected intelligent systems.
paragraphs: An NSERC Discovery Grant supports the lab’s work on scalable, reliable and robust provenance in interconnected intelligent systems.
The lab announced the grant in March 2024.

news.title: O-RAN research in IEEE Communications Magazine
news.summary: Research on signaling storms in open radio access networks.
paragraphs: “Signaling Storm in O-RAN: Challenges and Research Opportunities” appeared in IEEE Communications Magazine.
The work considers signaling storms in open radio access networks. The lab shared the publication update in December 2023.
